_about: Raw JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio between capture_wire.py (a bare client, no SDK, no model) and the ingredient-db server, captured 2026-09-24 by `python capture_wire.py ingredient-db lookup_nutrition '{"ingredient": "urad dal"}'`. Each 'raw' value is the exact line written to or read from the pipe; 'annotations' covers every top-level field of that message. Transport: newline-delimited JSON on the server's stdin/stdout; the server's logs go to stderr.
model_call_location: The model is called only in the host (mcp_agent.py, _gemini_step -> client.interactions.create); it is never called in either MCP server or anywhere in this exchange - initialize, tools/list and tools/call are answered by deterministic code, and this client declared no sampling capability, so the server has no way to request one.

annotations.jsonrpc: Protocol envelope. Always the string "2.0"; every MCP message is a JSON-RPC 2.0 message.
annotations.id: Request id 1, chosen by the client. The server must echo it so the reply can be matched. Its presence is what makes this a request rather than a notification.
annotations.method: "initialize" - must be the first request on a connection. Nothing else is answered until it completes.
annotations.params: protocolVersion: the newest spec revision the client speaks (2025-11-25). capabilities: {} - this client offers nothing back to the server (no sampling, no roots, no elicitation), so the server cannot ask the host to run a model. clientInfo: name/version, for logs only.

annotations.id: 1 - echoes the request, so this is the reply to initialize.
annotations.result: capabilities: what the server supports - tools (listChanged:false: its tool list never changes mid-session, so the host need not re-list), resources (subscribe:false, listChanged:false), prompts, experimental {}. protocolVersion: the server agreed to 2025-11-25; had it not supported it, it would answer a version it does support and the client decides whether to continue. serverInfo: name "ingredient-db", version "" - the server declares no version, so a host cannot pin or audit which release it is talking to (noted in risk_note.md). No 'instructions' field was sent.

annotations.method: "notifications/initialized" - the client confirms the handshake is done; normal requests may follow.
annotations.(no id): Deliberately absent: a notification gets no response. That is why the capture shows no server line for this step.

annotations.method: "tools/list" - discovery. This is the only place the host learns what tools exist; mcp_agent.py builds the model's tool list from exactly this reply.
annotations.(no params): Omitted: no pagination cursor on the first page.

exchange.raw: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"tools":[{"description":"Look up which allergen flags one ingredient carries.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"ingredient":{"description":"Ingredient name, e.g. 'urad dal' or 'Thick sour curd'.","title":"Ingredient","type":"string"}},"required":["ingredient"],"type":"object","title":"lookup_allergensArguments"},"name":"lookup_allergens","outputSchema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true,"title":"lookup_allergensDictOutput"}},{"description":"Look up per-100g nutrition (energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, fibre, sodium) for one\n    ingredient, by raw weight.","inputSchema":{"properties":{"ingredient":{"description":"Ingredient name, e.g. 'urad dal' or 'Thick sour curd'.","title":"Ingredient","type":"string"}},"required":["ingredient"],"type":"object","title":"lookup_nutritionArguments"},"name":"lookup_nutrition","outputSchema":{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true,"title":"lookup_nutritionDictOutput"}}]}}

annotations.result: tools: 2 entries, lookup_allergens and lookup_nutrition. Per tool: name (what the model calls); description (the Python docstring, verbatim, including its newline and indentation - this text IS the prompt the model reads); inputSchema (JSON Schema generated from the type hints; 'title' keys are SDK noise that mcp_agent.py strips before handing it to the model); outputSchema (a loose object schema auto-derived from the '-> dict' return hint - says almost nothing). No nextCursor, so this is the complete list. NOT on the wire, although the SDK's parsed object shows them: ttlMs, cacheScope, resultType - those are client-side defaults.

annotations.method: "tools/call" - invoke one tool. In the agent, the model chose this call; here this script sends it by hand, which proves the server needs no model to answer it.
annotations.params: name: "lookup_nutrition", one of the names tools/list returned. arguments: {"ingredient": "urad dal"} - validated by the server against the inputSchema before the function runs. The raw user query text reaches the server here, and it is written to vendor/ingredient_db/queries.log.

annotations.result: content: one text block holding the result as pretty-printed JSON - this is what mcp_agent.py passes to the model as the function_result. isError: false - a tool-level success flag, separate from a JSON-RPC 'error' member (which would mean the protocol call itself failed). The agent maps it straight onto Gemini's is_error. structuredContent: the same result as a JSON object, for hosts that want data rather than text. Note the fuzzy match: the query was 'urad dal', the record returned is 'Whole white urad dal' - the server resolved an alias, and says so in the 'ingredient' field.
